ads.description:
Most people think lead gen = buy a list. However the winners are the ones who can manufacture live intelligence on demand. That’s what this video is about.

Not “how to use Clay” or “a neat Sales Navigator trick.”

It’s about building a system where:

Hiring signals become triggers.
Company data gets de-duped and structured.
Titles and org charts are mapped in minutes.

Contacts are pulled and enriched across tools like Clay, Sales Nav, PhantomBuster, and LeadMagic.

What used to take an agency days now takes 15 minutes if you think like an operator.

That’s the bigger point here. Outbound isn’t about tools.

It’s about stitching together SIGNALS to build LISTS of CONTACTS that you have RELEVANT MESSAGING for.... into a continuous cycle of intelligent outreach.

Most teams are still playing checkers here. I've seen it. They’re buying static lists, maybe 1 data provider and clicking filters, maybe some burning of credits if they're lucky, and then blasting noise.

Meanwhile, operators who work like this are running laps around them.
Watch the walkthrough. More importantly, steal the philosophy.

The future of outbound won’t be won by the flashiest tech stack. It’ll be won by whoever can use it to turn signals into conversations the fastest.

ads.description:
90% of your ChatGPT prompts fail.

Here's Why:

You're guessing prompts, not planning them strategically.

Stop wasting time and learn.

In this cheatsheet, I break down the basics.

There's much more, but this is enough to be dangerous.

This approach turned simple ChatGPT instructions into a profitable SaaS business.

I didn't learn "how to code," "hire 1,000 developers," or "raise millions from investors."

I simply learned how to plan and execute with AI & Tools.

Prompting is fundamental for your success it certainly was for mine.

Basic Prompt Techniques:

☑ Zero-shot Prompting: Clear, direct instructions.
☑ Role Prompting: Assign ChatGPT specific roles.

Advanced Prompt Techniques:

☑ Few-shot Prompting: Provide examples to guide outputs.
☑ Action-Word Prompting: Use verbs to shape precise responses.
☑ Chain-of-Thought Prompting: Break complex tasks into clear, sequential steps.
☑ Self-consistency Prompting: Request multiple variations, then carefully select the strongest answer.

Essentials for Powerful Prompts:
☑ Clear Goals: Explicitly state your desired outcome.
☑ Action Words: Strong verbs drive actionable results.
☑ Context Wins: Specify details—role, tone, audience, style.
☑ Precision Matters: Numbers & constraints boost accuracy.
☑ Iterate & Refine: Continuously review, test, and optimize prompts.

The next guide I'll put out will be on "Reasoning" models.

They're a game changer.

With these, you can use one prompt and build an entire software platform.

Great prompts aren't magic - they're carefully structured commands.

Just built a microsite with examples from the cheatsheet.

Has advanced examples, which wouldn't fit on here.

Do you want me to send it?

Just comment "PROMPTS" and I'll send the link.

ads.description:
Still not seeing what Clay can really do?

You’re probably not thinking big enough.

The best users treat Clay like a GTM Command Center.

The rest?  

Like a colorful spreadsheet.

Some even try to attack it because it's popular.

Those people are far from reality.

Let me help you try to figure out where you might land.

I’ve helped teams build entire prospecting engines inside Clay powered by APIs and creativity.

We partner with Clay and many customers use LeadMagic inside Clay.

Clay removes the hard parts of using tech to prospect, research, and trigger.

And many other things if you can get there.

It’s full automation.

It's like being able to spend 20-30 minutes researching every prospect you have in your system. 

(🦾Eric Nowoslawski mentions this on his YouTube channel alot)

Then executing the campaign flawlessly.

Just like your best rep wrote it up.

And the only limit? 

Your imagination.

And your ability to convince your boss you're worth a few Clay Credits to get some momentum.

It's insane leverage for GTM teams.

☑ Clay is not just data enrichment
→ It’s trigger events, live workflows, creative logic

→ The best GTM teams use Clay to build:
• Scorecards
• Routing logic
• Email waterfalls
 • Lead scoring systems

→ The power is in chaining ideas, not just pulling inputs

☑ The others? 

They open it once... then run back to Excel & Ops Team for help.

Clay is a creativity unlock.

Not a plug-and-play template.

It’s a blank page and superpowers.

Clay makes every website an API for GTM professionals.

And the more creative your brain is, the more powerful the technology is.

Steve Jobs once said the personal computer is the bicycle of the mind.

I think Clay is that for Go-to-Market teams.

Need some creativity?

I built a microsite of 13 use cases with shared templates and SOPs (by role).

Want it?

PS: Comment “BICYCLE” and I'll send you the link.

ads.description:
Most SaaS Founders are WRONG about bootstrapping.

Growing slowly can hurt more than it helps.

The two trends I keep seeing:

“It's too risky.”
“I can just make $2k/month and survive.”

Neither of these are true.

Let's look at the math.

Currently, for every 1,000 Go-to-Market (GTM) professionals, about 10 leave their jobs to launch their own businesses.

Soon, that'll increase 5x.  (my prediction)

Meaning, for every 1,000 GTM professionals, 50 will step out on their own.

Your favorite feature will already be in a SaaS before you even think about launching.

Start today.

In just 2 minutes, I'll break it down for you.

I built my first SaaS without investors.

It was tough—but taught me exactly what works (and what doesn’t):

☑ Validation: Test fast, fix quick.
 → Growth: Spend less, earn more, keep control.
 ↳ Sustainability: Stay healthy, grow steady, last longer.

BUT: Slow growth isn’t always safe—it can kill your momentum.

 AND: Raising money isn't always bad—it might speed your success.

Bootstrapping isn't right for everyone, and that's OK.

My first $30k/MRR came from a No-Code MVP—when we simply opened our Agency Portal to the public.

The agency was doing fine, but not taking investors was risky. I had to move fast.

Today, building something valuable is even easier.

What took me 3 months then would take 3 hours now. Scary.

I'd ship a new product before most people see it in their feed.

What's your biggest fear about building SaaS products today?

If you're an Agency Owner or GTM Engineer, why not become an AI Engineer 
and figure it out?

Eventually, giving away all your best Clay Tables on the first call gets old.

PS: I put together a few tech stacks I'd recommend.  Just comment "tech stack" so I know and can send it.

♻️ if you want others to see this great guide

ads.description:
Your cold email game is outdated.

The gurus might not like this but...

It's time for you to consider a refresh.

Most Agencies are failing because they're not focusing on the fundamentals.

🦾Eric Nowoslawski put out his recent GEX 2024 report and talked about all things he saw related to Cold Email.

I've compiled it into a Cheat Sheet with the help of Vaibhav Namburi, Max Mitcham, and Nick Abraham.

We collaborate all the time on tactics/strategy and felt it was important to share it with everyone.

The best agencies have a strict process + system they use to scale.

We now have over 800+ agencies now find and validate emails and clean their data.

Plus, I've been deeply involved with the SmartLead team in building their product to get the best reply rates.

Here are some of the key learnings:

✅ Subject Lines: Keep it to 3 words max. 
✅ Clear Value: Each email should offer exactly one clear benefit. 
✅ Social Triggers: Reference recent funding, LinkedIn activities, or mutual connections to boost relevance. 
✅ Problem-Focused: Directly address specific pain points your prospect is facing.

Example:

"3-word subject lines only." 
→ Clear value: "Offer one clear benefit per email." 
↳ Social triggers: "Use recent funding or LinkedIn engagement." 
➜ Problem-solve: "Identify pain clearly; offer solutions, not features." 
✔ Follow-ups win: "New angles every 3 days close deals faster than pressure.

Most agencies ignore these basics, chasing flashy tactics instead. Fundamentals always win.

Want the full breakdown? 

Eric Nowoslawski just released an in-depth cheat sheet. (GEX 2024 Report)

If you missed it just comment "GEX" and I'll send it to you.

♻️ Reshare if you found this valuable.
